pr.title: perf(prims-ts): compute each work tile's visible K range once for softmax masking
pr.body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Every Prims-TS softmax now chooses between its masked and unmasked path the same way. It computes the work tile's visible K range once (in the task cache, SMEM or the work tile), then makes one comparison per K tile. Before this PR, several paths rebuilt their bounds on every tile, reloaded request metadata from GMEM, or masked every tile.

- **Shared helpers** (`kernels/mask.py`):
  - `unmasked_kv_tile_range` / `kv_tile_in_range` (plus a packed one-word form) build and test the range.
  - `kv_tile_needs_right_mask` / `kv_tile_is_fully_visible` are the key-space forms, for bounds already live in the loop.
- **FMHA context:**
  - Variable-window, sliding-window and head-paired varlen LOOP masks cache a per-warp tile range in SMEM, packed into one 32-bit word. They used to mask every tile.
  - Query-paired causal and packed dense-K use the shared right-bound test.
  - TAIL masks are unchanged.
- **FMHA decode:**
  - Grouped per-row causal and sliding-window CTAs cache their visible K interval (end, plus begin for a window) in the task cache.
  - The FP8 Q128 streamed Swaps path compared every score on every tile; it now masks only boundary tiles, in one pass per Q32 band.
- **MLA decode:**
  - When the rows of one tile see different prefixes, the tile caches its first row's K prefix once. This covers causal MTP and packed-Q (`qo_indptr`), in both 1CTA and 2CTA, and context-parallel causal in 2CTA, which previously masked every tile. Per-row bounds load only on masked tiles.
  - The 1CTA dense test drops a `seq_len % tile` term that masked every tile of an unaligned request.

The D256 LDTM.STAT context softmax is the one deliberate exception to "cache once". Every loop-carried form of its causal bound regressed 3–8%, because ptxas copied the 128-register S tile on every tile. So that bound is rebuilt each tile from values already in registers. That compiles to main's instruction count. The reason is recorded in the code and in the commit message.

**Performance** (B300, `253986e2d` vs this branch at `ba0560642`, outputs bitwise identical in every case). These come from the new [mask-tile A/B suite](https://github.com/PerkzZheng/flashinfer-prims-ts-validation/blob/main/docs/mask_tiles.md): 33 cases, 5 interleaved rounds, median paired ratio, geomean −2.98%.

| Case | main µs | PR µs | Δ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| context, sliding window 1024, S=8K | 135.2 | 108.0 | −20.1% |
| context, sliding window 4000, S=8K | 351.1 | 267.6 | −23.7% |
| context, variable window 2048, S=4K | 211.9 | 179.0 | −15.6% |
| context, packed sliding window 2048, S_kv > S_q | 591.1 | 459.8 | −22.2% |
| MLA H128, context parallel 8×64, packed-Q causal | 120.2 | 118.1 | −2.1% |
| MLA H128, context parallel 8×64, causal MTP (SQ4) | 141.5 | 139.7 | −1.2% |
| context, paged shifted causal D256 (4 shapes) | — | — | −0.21% … +0.02% |
| worst case of the 33 (MLA H16 packed-Q causal) | 54.7 | 55.2 | +0.9% |

Measured separately on the same GPU, interleaved against main:
- FP8 Q128 streamed Swaps path, forced: −3.3% / −4.5%.
- `flashinfer_benchmark.py` MLA matrix, 70 cases: geomean −0.14%. The 11 cases above +0.5% were re-run for 8 rounds; all are ≤ +0.9%.
- D256 shifted-causal paged context, 6 shapes × 5 rounds: −0.9% … +0.2%.

def _missing_jit_cache_spec_info(spec: JitSpec) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Return report metadata without assuming a particular JIT backend."""
    if isinstance(spec, JitSpecNvcc):

def _set_torch_compile_options():
    import torch._dynamo.config

    torch._dynamo.config.cache_size_limit = 128


def _monkeypatch_add_torch_compile(func):
    """
    Replace the given function with its torch.compile version.
    """

    from torch._library.custom_ops import CustomOpDef

    if type(func) is types.FunctionType:
        fn = func
    elif isinstance(func, CustomOpDef):
        fn = func._init_fn
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported fn type {type(func)}")

    fullname = fn.__module__ + "." + fn.__qualname__
    components = fullname.split(".")
    assert components[0] == "flashinfer"
    module = flashinfer
    for component in components[1:-1]:
        module = getattr(module, component)
    if not hasattr(module, components[-1]):
        raise ValueError(f"Failed to monkeypatch: {fullname}")

    def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
        compiled = _TORCH_COMPILE_CACHE.get(fullname)
        if compiled is None:
            # Warmup -- JIT compile / import the kernels.
            #
            # From user side, users also need to warmup the model beforehand,
            # as suggested by PyTorch Cuda Graph docs (not sure if it's also
            # recommended for torch.compile as well.)
            #
            # For the convenience of FlashInfer testing, we do the warmup here,
            # on the first run of the function. The caveat is that the first
            # call will run twice: once to warmup, and another through the
            # compiled version.
            func(*args, **kwargs)

            # Compile
            compiled = torch.compile(
                func,
                fullgraph=True,
                backend="inductor",
                mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs",
            )
            _TORCH_COMPILE_CACHE[fn.__name__] = compiled

        return compiled(*args, **kwargs)

    setattr(module, fn.__name__, wrapper)
    print("Applied torch.compile to", fullname)

                    "check install log for skipped-backend warnings)"

                item.add_marker(

def is_cuda_oom_error_str(e: str) -> bool:
    return "CUDA" in e and "out of memory" in e


def _release_cuda_oom(e: BaseException) -> bool:
    """Return whether ``e`` or a linked exception is a CUDA OOM; if so, free its frames.

    torch.testing.assert_close re-raises an OOM from inside its comparison as a
    RuntimeError caused by the OOM, so both ``__cause__`` and ``__context__`` are
    followed. The skip exception keeps these exceptions alive, and their
    tracebacks would keep the test's frames and GPU tensors allocated into the
    tests that follow.
    """
    chain: list[BaseException] = []
    pending: list[BaseException | None] = [e]
    while pending:
        x = pending.pop()
        if x is None or any(x is seen for seen in chain):
            continue
        chain.append(x)
        pending += [x.__cause__, x.__context__]
    if not any(
        isinstance(x, torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError) or is_cuda_oom_error_str(str(x))
        for x in chain
    ):
        return False
    for x in chain:
        traceback.clear_frames(x.__traceback__)
    return True


@pytest.hookimpl(wrapper=True)
def pytest_runtest_call(item):
    # skip OOM error and missing JIT cache errors
    try:
        yield
    except (torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError, RuntimeError) as e:
        if os.environ.get("FLASHINFER_STRICT_MOE_EP_TESTS") == "1":
            raise
        if _release_cuda_oom(e):
            pytest.skip("Skipping due to OOM")
        elif isinstance(e, MissingJITCacheError):
            # Record the test that was skipped due to missing JIT cache
            test_name = item.nodeid
            spec = e.spec
            module_name = spec.name if spec else "unknown"

            # Create a dict with module info for reporting
            spec_info = _missing_jit_cache_spec_info(spec) if spec else None

            _MISSING_JIT_CACHE_MODULES.add((test_name, module_name, str(spec_info)))
            pytest.skip(f"Skipping due to missing JIT cache for module: {module_name}")
        else:
            raise


def pytest_terminal_summary(terminalreporter, exitstatus, config):
    """Generate JIT cache coverage report at the end of test session"""
    if not _MISSING_JIT_CACHE_MODULES:
        return  # No missing modules

    # If report file is specified, write to file for later aggregation
    # Otherwise, print summary directly
    if _JIT_CACHE_REPORT_FILE:
        from filelock import FileLock

        # Convert set to list for JSON serialization
        data = [
            {"test_name": test_name, "module_name": module_name, "spec_info": spec_info}
            for test_name, module_name, spec_info in _MISSING_JIT_CACHE_MODULES
        ]

        # Use file locking to handle concurrent writes from multiple pytest processes
        Path(_JIT_CACHE_REPORT_FILE).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        lock_file = _JIT_CACHE_REPORT_FILE + ".lock"
        with FileLock(lock_file), open(_JIT_CACHE_REPORT_FILE, "a") as f:
            for entry in data:
                f.write(json.dumps(entry) + "\n")
        return

    # Single pytest run - print summary directly
    terminalreporter.section("flashinfer-jit-cache Package Coverage Report")
    terminalreporter.write_line("")
    terminalreporter.write_line(
        "This report shows the coverage of the flashinfer-jit-cache package."
    )
    terminalreporter.write_line(
        "Tests are skipped when required modules are not found in the installed JIT cache."
    )
    terminalreporter.write_line("")
    terminalreporter.write_line(
        f"⚠️  {len(_MISSING_JIT_CACHE_MODULES)} test(s) skipped due to missing JIT cache modules:"
    )
    terminalreporter.write_line("")

    # Group by module name
    module_to_tests = {}
    for test_name, module_name, spec_info in _MISSING_JIT_CACHE_MODULES:
        if module_name not in module_to_tests:
            module_to_tests[module_name] = {"tests": [], "spec_info": spec_info}
        module_to_tests[module_name]["tests"].append(test_name)

    for module_name in sorted(module_to_tests.keys()):
        info = module_to_tests[module_name]
        terminalreporter.write_line(f"Module: {module_name}")
        terminalreporter.write_line(f"  Spec: {info['spec_info']}")
        terminalreporter.write_line(f"  Affected tests ({len(info['tests'])}):")
        for test in sorted(info["tests"]):
            terminalreporter.write_line(f"    - {test}")
        terminalreporter.write_line("")

    terminalreporter.write_line(
        "These tests require JIT compilation but FLASHINFER_DISABLE_JIT=1 was set."
    )
    terminalreporter.write_line(
        "To improve coverage, add the missing modules to the flashinfer-jit-cache build configuration."
    )

            return "${runner_exit_code}"
            ;;
    esac

    case "${runner_exit_code}" in
        0|2)

            ;;

            return "${runner_exit_code}"

"""Shared masking predicates for PrimTS attention kernels.

Every PrimTS softmax follows one masking design::

    once per work tile:   [begin, end) = unmasked_kv_tile_range(...)
    once per KV tile:     masked = not kv_tile_in_range(tile_idx, begin, end)
                          (or packed_kv_tile_in_range on one packed word)

      KV tiles   0 .. begin-1 | begin ........ end-1 | end .. N-1
                 left-masked  |  unmasked (no mask)  | right-masked

The range is the intersection of every row's visible key interval in the
work tile, rounded inward to whole tiles, in absolute KV tile indices. It
is computed once, before the KV loop, from the work tile's geometry
(sequence lengths, causal offset, sliding window, explicit K bounds), so a
KV tile pays one range test instead of rebuilding row bounds. A kernel
whose single right bound is already live in the loop compares it in key
space instead (``kv_tile_needs_right_mask``), which needs no extra
loop-carried state. Masked tiles
keep their exact per-row/per-key mask code; unmasked tiles take a
specialization without it. Data-dependent sparse masks (sparse routes,
page-membership words) are outside this range test and keep their own
predicates.

All helpers accept Python integers (host-side tests, trace-time constants)
or CuTe DSL integer values (device code). Intervals are half-open.
"""


def _imax(a, b):
    """Return ``max(a, b)`` for Python or CuTe DSL integers."""
    if isinstance(a, int) and isinstance(b, int):
        return max(a, b)
    import cutlass.cute as cute
    from cutlass import Int32

    return cute.math.max(Int32(a), Int32(b))


def _imin(a, b):
    """Return ``min(a, b)`` for Python or CuTe DSL integers."""
    if isinstance(a, int) and isinstance(b, int):
        return min(a, b)
    import cutlass.cute as cute
    from cutlass import Int32

    return cute.math.min(Int32(a), Int32(b))


def unmasked_kv_tile_range(visible_k_begin, visible_k_end, tile_size_kv):
    """Return the absolute KV tile range ``[begin, end)`` that needs no mask.

    ``visible_k_begin`` is the largest left bound and ``visible_k_end`` the
    smallest right bound over every row of the work tile, so a tile inside
    ``[visible_k_begin, visible_k_end)`` is visible to all rows. ``begin``
    rounds the left bound up and ``end`` rounds the right bound down to a
    tile edge; an empty intersection yields ``begin == end`` (every tile is
    masked).
    """
    begin_k = _imax(visible_k_begin, 0)
    end_k = _imax(visible_k_end, 0)
    begin = (begin_k + (tile_size_kv - 1)) // tile_size_kv
    end = _imax(end_k // tile_size_kv, begin)
    return begin, end


def kv_tile_in_range(tile_idx, begin, end):
    """Return whether absolute KV tile ``tile_idx`` lies in ``[begin, end)``.

    With ``[begin, end)`` from :func:`unmasked_kv_tile_range`, true selects
    the unmasked specialization.
    """
    return (tile_idx >= begin) & (tile_idx < end)


def kv_tile_needs_right_mask(tile_offset_k, tile_size_kv, visible_k_end):
    """Return whether a KV tile crosses a row-visible right bound.

    The key-space form of the range test, for kernels whose right bound is
    already live in the KV loop: comparing it against the tile's first key
    adds no loop-carried register, where a cached tile range would.
    """
    return tile_offset_k + tile_size_kv > visible_k_end


def kv_tile_is_fully_visible(
    tile_offset_k,
    tile_size_kv,
    visible_k_begin,
    visible_k_end,
):
    """Return whether a KV tile is inside every row's visible interval.

    The key-space form of the range test for a two-sided interval whose
    bounds are already live in the KV loop. All intervals are half-open.
    """
    return (tile_offset_k >= visible_k_begin) & (
        tile_offset_k + tile_size_kv <= visible_k_end
    )


_PACKED_TILE_MAX = 0xFFFF


def pack_kv_tile_range(begin, end):
    """Pack a tile range ``[begin, end)`` into one 32-bit word, ``end << 16 | begin``.

    Kernels whose softmax registers are at their budget carry the range
    through the KV loop as one live value instead of two. Both bounds are
    clamped to 65535, which only shrinks the range: an open or far right bound
    keeps tiles from 65535 on masked, and a range starting there is empty.
    """
    begin = _imin(begin, _PACKED_TILE_MAX)
    end = _imin(end, _PACKED_TILE_MAX)
    return (end << 16) | begin


def packed_kv_tile_in_range(tile_idx, packed_range):
    """Return whether ``tile_idx`` lies in a range packed by :func:`pack_kv_tile_range`.

    The 32-bit word may be negative, so the upper field is decoded unsigned.
    """
    return kv_tile_in_range(
        tile_idx,
        packed_range & _PACKED_TILE_MAX,
        (packed_range >> 16) & _PACKED_TILE_MAX,
    )

def test_unmasked_kv_tile_range_matches_per_tile_visibility() -> None:
    """The cached tile range, plain or packed, selects exactly the fully visible tiles.

    The packed word is read back as a signed 32-bit register, as on the GPU.
    Bounds past its 16-bit fields may only shrink the range.
    """
    pytest.importorskip("cutlass", minversion="4.7.0")
    from flashinfer.attention.prims_ts.kernels.mask import (
        kv_tile_in_range,
        kv_tile_is_fully_visible,
        pack_kv_tile_range,
        packed_kv_tile_in_range,
        unmasked_kv_tile_range,
    )

    def as_int32(word: int) -> int:
        word &= 0xFFFFFFFF
        return word - (1 << 32) if word >= 1 << 31 else word

    for tile_size_kv in (1, 3, 128):
        for visible_begin in range(-130, 400, 7):
            for visible_end in range(-130, 400, 11):
                begin, end = unmasked_kv_tile_range(

                packed = as_int32(pack_kv_tile_range(begin, end))
                for tile_idx in range(400 // tile_size_kv + 2):
                    visible = kv_tile_is_fully_visible(
                        tile_idx * tile_size_kv,

                        visible_begin,
                        visible_end,
                    )
                    assert kv_tile_in_range(tile_idx, begin, end) is visible
                    assert packed_kv_tile_in_range(tile_idx, packed) is visible

    for begin, end in ((5, 0x8000), (5, 0x3FFFFFFF // 128), (0x10000, 0x10001)):
        packed = as_int32(pack_kv_tile_range(begin, end))
        for tile_idx in (0, 5, 0x7FFF, 0xFFFE, 0xFFFF, 0x10000):

def _make_bounded_case(
    *,
    num_heads: int = 96,
    seq_len_q: int = 6,
    kv_lengths: tuple[int, ...] = (0, 65, 257),
    qkv_dtype: torch.dtype = torch.bfloat16,
    mask_type: str = "causal",
    page_size: int = 64,
    device: str = "cuda",
) -> _MLACase:
    """Reuse shuffled pages while allowing empty rank-local KV sequences."""

    capacity = max(page_size, max(kv_lengths))
    case = _make_mla_case(
        batch_size=len(kv_lengths),
        num_qo_heads=num_heads,
        max_kv_len=capacity,
        seq_len_q=seq_len_q,
        kv_seq_lens=(capacity,) * len(kv_lengths),
        qkv_dtype=qkv_dtype,
        mask_type="dense",
        page_size=page_size,
        device=device,
        seed=62100 + num_heads + seq_len_q,
    )
    return replace(
        case,
        seq_lens_kv=torch.tensor(kv_lengths, dtype=torch.int32, device=device),
        mask_type=mask_type,
    )


def _plan_cp(

    wrapper.plan(

        case.query.shape[-2],
        _LATENT_DIM,

        cp_world=cp_world,

    assert wrapper._plan_state.cp_world == cp_world

    assert callable(wrapper._plan_state.compiled)

def _run_cp(

def _cp_reference_inputs(
    case: _MLACase,
    global_lengths: torch.Tensor,
    *,
    cp_rank: int,
    cp_world: int,
    cp_interleave_size: int,
    qo_indptr: torch.Tensor | None = None,
) -> tuple[_MLACase, torch.Tensor]:
    """Enumerate global ownership independently of the kernel prefix formula."""
    q_lengths = (
        (qo_indptr[1:] - qo_indptr[:-1]).tolist()
        if qo_indptr is not None
        else [case.query.shape[1]] * case.block_tables.shape[0]
    )
    local_lengths, bounds = [], []
    for length, q_len in zip(global_lengths.tolist(), q_lengths, strict=True):
        positions = torch.arange(length, device=case.query.device)
        owned = positions[(positions // cp_interleave_size) % cp_world == cp_rank]
        local_lengths.append(owned.numel())
        for q_idx in range(q_len):
            endpoint = (
                length if case.mask_type == "dense" else length - q_len + q_idx + 1
            )
            bounds.append(int((owned < endpoint).sum().item()))
    return (
        replace(
            case,
            seq_lens_kv=torch.tensor(
                local_lengths, dtype=torch.int32, device=case.query.device
            ),
        ),
        torch.tensor(bounds, dtype=torch.int32, device=case.query.device),
    )


@torch.no_grad()
def _bounded_reference(
    case: _MLACase,
    bounds: torch.Tensor,
    *,
    qo_indptr: torch.Tensor | None = None,
    policy: dict[str, object] | None = None,
    bf16_single_tile: bool = False,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute base-2 LSE and model the selected low-precision PV operands."""

    query = case.query.reshape(-1, case.query.shape[-2], case.query.shape[-1])
    output = torch.zeros(
        (*query.shape[:-1], _LATENT_DIM), dtype=torch.float32, device=query.device
    )
    stats = torch.full(
        query.shape[:-1], -torch.inf, dtype=torch.float32, device=query.device
    )
    offsets = (
        qo_indptr.tolist()
        if qo_indptr is not None
        else list(range(0, query.shape[0] + 1, case.query.shape[1]))
    )
    bound_values = bounds.tolist()
    for batch_idx, (begin, end) in enumerate(
        zip(offsets[:-1], offsets[1:], strict=True)
    ):
        cache = _gather_request_cache(case, batch_idx)
        for query_idx in range(begin, end):
            visible = int(bound_values[query_idx])
            if visible == 0:
                continue
            visible_cache = cache[:visible]
            logits = query[query_idx].float() @ visible_cache.T * case.softmax_scale
            maximum = logits.max(dim=-1).values
            weights = torch.exp(logits - maximum[:, None])
            denominator = weights.sum(dim=-1)
            if case.query.dtype == _FP8 and policy is not None:
                output[query_idx] = _fp8_request_reference(
                    query[query_idx].float(),
                    cache,
                    softmax_scale=case.softmax_scale,
                    output_scale=case.output_scale,
                    num_insts_kv=int(policy["num_insts_kv"]),
                    tile_size_kv=int(policy["tile_size_kv"]),
                    splits_kv=int(policy["split_kv"]),
                    visible_kv_len=visible,
                )
            else:
                probabilities = weights
                if bf16_single_tile:
                    # This BF16 oracle covers one KV tile, without online or
                    # split rescaling. PV rounds P; the denominator does not.
                    assert case.query.dtype == torch.bfloat16 and policy is not None
                    assert cache.shape[0] <= int(policy["tile_size_kv"])
                    assert int(policy["split_kv"]) == 1
                    assert int(policy["num_insts_kv"]) == 1
                    probabilities = weights.to(torch.bfloat16).float()
                output[query_idx] = (
                    probabilities
                    @ visible_cache[:, :_LATENT_DIM]
                    / denominator[:, None]
                    * case.output_scale
                )
            stats[query_idx] = logits.logsumexp(-1) / math.log(2)
    return (
        output.reshape(*case.query.shape[:-1], _LATENT_DIM),
        stats.reshape(case.query.shape[:-1]),
    )


def _assert_output_reference(
    output: torch.Tensor,
    expected: torch.Tensor,
    fp32_expected: torch.Tensor,
    *,
    dtype: torch.dtype,
) -> None:
    rtol, atol = _mla_tolerances(dtype)
    torch.testing.assert_close(output.float(), expected, rtol=rtol, atol=atol)
    if dtype == _FP8:
        expected_norm = torch.linalg.vector_norm(fp32_expected)
        error_norm = torch.linalg.vector_norm(output.float() - fp32_expected)
        # P448 rounding is checked elementwise above. Keep an independent
        # mathematical-attention quality gate, including exact all-zero output.
        assert float(error_norm) <= 0.05 * float(expected_norm)


def _merge_reference(
    output: torch.Tensor, stats: torch.Tensor
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    maximum = stats.max(dim=0).values
    mass = torch.exp2(stats - maximum)
    denominator = mass.sum(dim=0)
    merged = (output.float() * mass[..., None]).sum(dim=0) / denominator[..., None]
    return merged, maximum + denominator.log2()


def _assert_bounded_result(
    case: _MLACase,
    bounds: torch.Tensor,
    output: torch.Tensor,
    stats: torch.Tensor,
    *,
    policy: dict[str, object],
    qo_indptr: torch.Tensor | None = None,
    bf16_single_tile: bool = False,
) -> None:
    expected_output, expected_stats = _bounded_reference(
        case,
        bounds,
        qo_indptr=qo_indptr,
        policy=policy,
        bf16_single_tile=bf16_single_tile,
    )
    assert output.dtype == case.out_dtype
    assert stats.dtype == torch.float32
    assert torch.isfinite(output).all()
    fp32_output = (
        _bounded_reference(case, bounds, qo_indptr=qo_indptr)[0]
        if case.query.dtype == _FP8
        else expected_output
    )
    _assert_output_reference(
        output, expected_output, fp32_output, dtype=case.query.dtype
    )
    torch.testing.assert_close(stats, expected_stats, rtol=2e-3, atol=2e-4)
    empty = bounds == 0
    flat_output = output.reshape(-1, output.shape[-2], _LATENT_DIM)
    flat_stats = stats.reshape(-1, stats.shape[-1])
    assert torch.count_nonzero(flat_output[empty]) == 0
    assert torch.isneginf(flat_stats[empty]).all()

def _run_cp_ranks(
    case: _MLACase, *, global_length: int, cp_world: int, cp_interleave_size: int
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, dict[str, object]]:
    """Run every rank through the same B=1 plan; rank must not specialize JIT."""

    def rank_case(rank):
        return replace(
            case,
            query=case.query[rank : rank + 1],
            block_tables=case.block_tables[rank : rank + 1],
            seq_lens_kv=case.seq_lens_kv[rank : rank + 1],
        )

    wrapper = _plan_cp(
        rank_case(0),
        max_q_len=case.query.shape[1],
        cp_world=cp_world,
        cp_interleave_size=cp_interleave_size,
    )
    compiled = wrapper._plan_state.compiled
    global_lengths = torch.tensor(
        [global_length], dtype=torch.int32, device=case.query.device
    )
    outputs, stats, all_bounds = [], [], []
    for rank in range(cp_world):
        local_case = rank_case(rank)
        local_case, bounds = _cp_reference_inputs(
            local_case,
            global_lengths,
            cp_rank=rank,
            cp_world=cp_world,
            cp_interleave_size=cp_interleave_size,
        )
        output, lse = _run_cp(wrapper, local_case, global_lengths, cp_rank=rank)
        _assert_bounded_result(
            local_case,
            bounds,
            output,
            lse,
            policy=_policy_dict(wrapper),
            bf16_single_tile=case.query.dtype == torch.bfloat16,
        )
        assert wrapper._plan_state.compiled is compiled
        outputs.append(output)
        stats.append(lse)
        all_bounds.append(bounds)
    return (
        torch.cat(outputs),
        torch.cat(stats),
        torch.cat(all_bounds),
        _policy_dict(wrapper),
    )


@_REQUIRES_PRIMTS_GPU
def test_attention_ts_mla_cp_helix_page_boundary() -> None:
    """BF16 PV rounding on short local prefixes must not corrupt LSE merging."""

    case = _make_bounded_case(
        seq_len_q=6, kv_lengths=(64, 5, 0), qkv_dtype=torch.bfloat16
    )
    case.query[1:].copy_(case.query[:1].expand(2, -1, -1, -1))
    output, stats, bounds, _ = _run_cp_ranks(
        case, global_length=69, cp_world=3, cp_interleave_size=64
    )
    assert bounds.tolist() == [64] * 6 + list(range(6)) + [0] * 6

    merged, merged_stats = _merge_reference(output, stats)
    global_cache = torch.cat([_gather_request_cache(case, rank) for rank in range(3)])
    expected_rows, expected_stats = [], []
    for row in range(6):
        visible = global_cache[: 64 + row]
        logits = case.query[0, row].float() @ visible.T * case.softmax_scale
        maximum = logits.max(dim=-1).values
        weights = torch.exp(logits - maximum[:, None])
        denominator = weights.sum(dim=-1)
        expected_rows.append(
            weights
            @ visible[:, :_LATENT_DIM]
            / denominator[:, None]
            * case.output_scale
        )
        expected_stats.append(logits.logsumexp(-1) / math.log(2))
    # Keep an independent mathematical-attention gate for the merged output.
    rtol, atol = _mla_tolerances(case.query.dtype)
    torch.testing.assert_close(merged, torch.stack(expected_rows), rtol=rtol, atol=atol)
    torch.testing.assert_close(
        merged_stats, torch.stack(expected_stats), rtol=2e-3, atol=2e-4
    )

@_REQUIRES_PRIMTS_GPU
def test_attention_ts_mla_cp8_page128(first_position: int) -> None:
    """Single-device CP8 page-interleaving and merge oracle for H96/Q8."""

    cp_size, page_size, seq_len_q = 8, 128, 8
    qkv_dtype = _FP8
    total_tokens = first_position + seq_len_q

    positions = torch.arange(total_tokens, device="cuda")
    owners = (positions // page_size) % cp_size
    kv_lengths = tuple(int((owners == rank).sum().item()) for rank in range(cp_size))
    case = _make_bounded_case(
        num_heads=96,
        seq_len_q=seq_len_q,
        kv_lengths=kv_lengths,
        qkv_dtype=qkv_dtype,
        page_size=page_size,
    )
    case.query[1:].copy_(case.query[:1].expand(cp_size - 1, -1, -1, -1))
    output, stats, bounds, policy = _run_cp_ranks(
        case, global_length=total_tokens, cp_world=cp_size, cp_interleave_size=page_size
    )
    assert policy["kernel"] == "throughput_2cta"
    per_rank_bounds = bounds.reshape(cp_size, seq_len_q)
    if first_position == 127:
        assert per_rank_bounds[:2, :3].tolist() == [[128, 128, 128], [0, 1, 2]]
        assert torch.count_nonzero(per_rank_bounds[2:]) == 0
    else:
        assert per_rank_bounds[0, :3].tolist() == [128, 129, 130]
        assert per_rank_bounds[7, :3].tolist() == [128, 128, 128]

    merged, merged_stats = _merge_reference(output, stats)
    local_expected, local_stats = _bounded_reference(case, bounds, policy=policy)
    quantized_merged, _ = _merge_reference(local_expected, local_stats)

    # CP8 wraps to rank zero at the ninth global page.
    global_cache = torch.empty(
        (total_tokens, case.query.shape[-1]), device=case.query.device
    )
    for rank in range(cp_size):
        global_cache[owners == rank] = _gather_request_cache(case, rank)
    expected_rows, expected_stats = [], []
    for q_idx in range(seq_len_q):
        visible = global_cache[: first_position + q_idx + 1]
        logits = case.query[0, q_idx].float() @ visible.T * case.softmax_scale
        row_maximum = logits.max(dim=-1).values
        weights = torch.exp(logits - row_maximum[:, None])
        row_sum = weights.sum(dim=-1)
        expected_rows.append(
            weights @ visible[:, :_LATENT_DIM] / row_sum[:, None] * case.output_scale
        )
        expected_stats.append(logits.logsumexp(-1) / math.log(2))
    _assert_output_reference(
        merged, quantized_merged, torch.stack(expected_rows), dtype=qkv_dtype
    )
    torch.testing.assert_close(
        merged_stats, torch.stack(expected_stats), rtol=2e-3, atol=2e-4
    )


def _exercise_cp_graph(
    case: _MLACase,
    initial: list[int],
    updated: list[int],
    *,
    max_q_len: int,
    cp_rank: int,
    cp_interleave_size: int,
    qo_indptr: torch.Tensor | None = None,
    updated_offsets: list[int] | None = None,
    expected_kernel: str | None = None,
    check_opt_out: bool = False,
) -> None:
    global_lengths = torch.tensor(initial, dtype=torch.int32, device=case.query.device)
    wrapper = _plan_cp(
        case,
        max_q_len=max_q_len,
        packed_query=qo_indptr is not None,
        cp_interleave_size=cp_interleave_size,
    )
    if expected_kernel is not None:
        assert _policy_dict(wrapper)["kernel"] == expected_kernel
    eager_output, eager_stats = _run_cp(
        wrapper, case, global_lengths, cp_rank=cp_rank, qo_indptr=qo_indptr
    )
    local_case, bounds = _cp_reference_inputs(
        case,
        global_lengths,
        cp_rank=cp_rank,
        cp_world=8,
        cp_interleave_size=cp_interleave_size,
        qo_indptr=qo_indptr,
    )
    _assert_bounded_result(
        local_case,
        bounds,
        eager_output,
        eager_stats,
        qo_indptr=qo_indptr,
        policy=_policy_dict(wrapper),
    )
    graph_out = torch.empty_like(eager_output)
    graph_stats = torch.empty_like(eager_stats)
    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
        captured, captured_stats = _run_cp(
            wrapper,
            case,
            global_lengths,
            cp_rank=cp_rank,
            qo_indptr=qo_indptr,
            out=graph_out,
            stats=graph_stats,
            validate=False,
        )
    assert captured is graph_out
    assert captured_stats is graph_stats
    lengths_ptr = global_lengths.data_ptr()
    original_pages = case.block_tables.clone()
    initial_offsets = qo_indptr.tolist() if qo_indptr is not None else None
    for values, offsets in (
        (updated, updated_offsets),
        ([0] * len(initial), updated_offsets),
        (initial, initial_offsets),
    ):
        global_lengths.copy_(torch.tensor(values, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"))
        if qo_indptr is not None:
            qo_indptr.copy_(torch.tensor(offsets, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"))
        local_case, bounds = _cp_reference_inputs(
            case,
            global_lengths,
            cp_rank=cp_rank,
            cp_world=8,
            cp_interleave_size=cp_interleave_size,
            qo_indptr=qo_indptr,
        )
        case.block_tables.copy_(original_pages)
        case.block_tables[local_case.seq_lens_kv == 0] = -1
        assert global_lengths.data_ptr() == lengths_ptr
        graph_out.fill_(float("nan"))
        graph_stats.fill_(float("nan"))
        graph.replay()
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        _assert_bounded_result(
            local_case,
            bounds,
            graph_out,
            graph_stats,
            qo_indptr=qo_indptr,
            policy=_policy_dict(wrapper),
        )
    _CUDA_GRAPH_ANCHOR_OWNERS.append(
        (graph, wrapper, case, global_lengths, qo_indptr, graph_out, graph_stats)
    )
    if check_opt_out:
        no_init = _plan_cp(
            case,
            max_q_len=max_q_len,
            packed_query=qo_indptr is not None,
            zero_empty_rows=False,
            cp_interleave_size=cp_interleave_size,
        )
        assert no_init._plan_state.compiled is not wrapper._plan_state.compiled
        assert (
            no_init._plan_state.workspace_layout == wrapper._plan_state.workspace_layout
        )
        output, stats = _run_cp(
            no_init, case, global_lengths, cp_rank=cp_rank, qo_indptr=qo_indptr
        )
        no_init_graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
        with torch.cuda.graph(no_init_graph):
            _run_cp(
                no_init,
                case,
                global_lengths,
                cp_rank=cp_rank,
                qo_indptr=qo_indptr,
                out=output,
                stats=stats,
                validate=False,
            )
        output.fill_(float("nan"))
        stats.fill_(float("nan"))
        no_init_graph.replay()
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        active = bounds > 0
        # Opt-out leaves empty rows unspecified; nonempty rows retain exact parity.
        torch.testing.assert_close(
            output.flatten(0, -3)[active],
            graph_out.flatten(0, -3)[active],
            rtol=0,
            atol=0,
        )
        torch.testing.assert_close(
            stats.reshape(-1, stats.shape[-1])[active],
            graph_stats.reshape(-1, graph_stats.shape[-1])[active],
            rtol=0,
            atol=0,
        )
        _CUDA_GRAPH_ANCHOR_OWNERS.append((no_init_graph, no_init, output, stats))

"""Policy tests for PrimTS and the legacy CSR paged-decode wrapper.

PrimTS decode consumes a dense page table directly. The legacy
``BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheWrapper`` remains CSR-shaped and therefore does
not expose a PrimTS backend. Numerical and CUDA-graph coverage for the direct
dense interface lives in ``test_attention_ts_decode.py``.
"""

import pytest
import torch

import flashinfer


requires_cuda = pytest.mark.skipif(
    not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="requires a CUDA device"
)


def _make_page_table(kv_lens, page_size, device):
    pages_per_req = [(kv_len + page_size - 1) // page_size for kv_len in kv_lens]
    offsets = [0]
    for num_pages in pages_per_req:
        offsets.append(offsets[-1] + num_pages)
    indptr = torch.tensor(offsets, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
    indices = torch.arange(sum(pages_per_req), dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
    last_page_len = torch.tensor(
        [
            kv_len - (num_pages - 1) * page_size
            for kv_len, num_pages in zip(kv_lens, pages_per_req, strict=True)
        ],
        dtype=torch.int32,
        device=device,
    )
    return indptr, indices, last_page_len


def _make_wrapper(backend, kv_layout="HND", device="cuda", **kwargs):
    workspace = torch.zeros(64 * 1024 * 1024, dtype=torch.uint8, device=device)
    return flashinfer.BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheWrapper(
        workspace, kv_layout, backend=backend, **kwargs
    )


@requires_cuda
def test_legacy_csr_wrapper_rejects_prims_ts_backend():
    with pytest.raises(
        NotImplementedError,
        match=r"dense.*BatchDecodePagedTSWrapper|BatchDecodePagedTSWrapper.*dense",
    ):
        _make_wrapper("prims-ts")


def test_plan_trace_captures_explicit_causal_mode():
    plan_trace = flashinfer.BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheWrapper.plan.fi_trace
    indptr, indices, last_page_len = _make_page_table([2, 3], 16, "cpu")
    definition = plan_trace(
        indptr=indptr,
        indices=indices,
        last_page_len=last_page_len,
        num_qo_heads=8,
        num_kv_heads=2,
        head_dim=128,
        page_size=16,
        kwargs={"q_len_per_req": 4, "is_causal": False},
    )

    assert definition["op_type"] == "gqa_paged_plan"
    assert definition["inputs"]["q_len_per_req"]["optional"] is True
    assert definition["inputs"]["is_causal"] == {
        "shape": None,
        "dtype": "bool",
        "optional": True,
        "description": "Whether the planned attention mask is causal.",
    }


@requires_cuda
@pytest.mark.parametrize("q_len_per_req,is_causal", [(4, False), (1, True)])
def test_explicit_is_causal_rejected_by_legacy_backends(q_len_per_req, is_causal):
    wrapper = _make_wrapper("fa2", kv_layout="NHD")
    indptr, indices, last_page_len = _make_page_table([64, 96], 16, "cuda")

            128,
            16,
            q_data_type=torch.bfloat16,

"""Mask policy shared by the MLA decode kernels and reference path."""

from enum import Enum

import cutlass
import cutlass.cute as cute
from cutlass import Int32


class MaskType(str, Enum):
    """Supported speculative-decode attention masks."""

    CAUSAL = "causal"
    DENSE = "dense"


def normalize_mask_type(mask_type: MaskType | str) -> str:
    """Return the canonical constexpr-safe string for ``mask_type``."""

    try:
        return MaskType(mask_type).value
    except (TypeError, ValueError) as error:
        supported = ", ".join(mask.value for mask in MaskType)
        raise ValueError(
            f"mask_type must be one of ({supported}), got {mask_type!r}"
        ) from error


def rows_have_distinct_kv_prefix(
    mask_type: str, runtime_q_lengths: bool, logical_seq_len_q
) -> bool:
    """Return whether the query rows of one tile can see different K prefixes.

    Bottom-right causal prefixes grow with the query token, so they differ
    unless every request has exactly one token. A work tile then caches the
    prefix its first row sees; otherwise every row sees the whole K length.
    """
    single_token = [redacted] runtime_q_lengths and (
        isinstance(logical_seq_len_q, int) and logical_seq_len_q == 1
    )
    return mask_type == MaskType.CAUSAL.value and not single_token


@cute.jit
def mask_visible_k_length(
    mask_type: cutlass.Constexpr[str],
    seq_len_kv,
    logical_q_idx,
    logical_seq_len_q,
):
    """Return the dense or bottom-right-causal K length for one Q row."""

    seq_len_kv = Int32(seq_len_kv)
    if cutlass.const_expr(mask_type == MaskType.DENSE.value):
        return cute.math.max(seq_len_kv, Int32(0))
    safe_seq_len_q = cute.math.max(Int32(logical_seq_len_q), Int32(1))
    safe_q_idx = cute.math.max(
        Int32(0),
        cute.math.min(Int32(logical_q_idx), safe_seq_len_q - Int32(1)),
    )
    return cute.math.max(
        seq_len_kv - (safe_seq_len_q - Int32(1) - safe_q_idx),
        Int32(0),
    )
